synopsis: Euro NCAP is an independent consumer-assessment body, not a regulator; its virtual-testing protocol version 1.00 was dated March 2025 and entered into force in January 2026, and its ratings do not constitute legal approval or regulatory evidence for machines [f1272, f15443, f2107]. The corpus identifies it as the clearest collision-avoidance precedent for external acceptance of simulation: manufacturers qualify models against physical tests using ISO scores and defined KPIs, submit a model dossier and full-grid predictions, and Euro NCAP physically verifies randomly selected cells [f1260, f15447, f15448]. Acceptance requires at least 75% of verification tests in each scenario cluster to meet qualification criteria; otherwise that cluster's dossier is rejected, with re-simulation or physical testing available [f15449]. Its permission to assume perfect perception limits its usefulness for sensor robustness, while unconfirmed ISO-score and KPI tolerances should not be copied as final off-road acceptance thresholds [f15451, f2502, f2503]. No off-road equivalent was found or adopted, so the booklet recommends using simulation as coverage and design evidence qualified against physical tests, rather than treating this consumer protocol as off-road approval [f346, f2507, f2143, f15443]. Planning must include credibility work beyond simulation runtime, but manufacturer-specific build and validation durations were not found; the research also reports that Euro NCAP virtual testing was not verified, qualifying confidence in its detailed account [f1565, f1273, f7702].
